excerpt: Introduced CBRN TCLs and outlined mitigation and risk acceptance process.
paraphrase: The 3.1 update added CBRN Tracked Capability Levels along with a mitigation and risk acceptance process.

excerpt: Incorporated the previous exploratory Misalignment risk domain into a combined ML R&D and Misalignment risk domain and outlined mitigation and risk acceptance process for the TCL.
paraphrase: The update merged the exploratory Misalignment domain with ML R&D into one combined domain and specified a mitigation and risk acceptance process for its TCL.

excerpt: Outlined enhanced level of security for CBRN, Cyber and Harmful Manipulation CCLs to Security Level 2+ to protect against non-state actors and insider threats.
paraphrase: The update specified an elevated security level, Security Level 2+, for CBRN, Cyber, and Harmful Manipulation CCLs to guard against non-state actors and insiders.

excerpt: Included more detail on our risk management process.
paraphrase: The update added further detail describing the risk management process.

excerpt: Included description of our internal governance structure.
paraphrase: The update added a description of the internal governance structure.

excerpt: Introduced a glossary.
paraphrase: The update added a glossary section.

excerpt: Version 3.0 (September 22, 2025)
paraphrase: Version 3.0 was released on September 22, 2025.

excerpt: Version 2.0 (February 4, 2025)
paraphrase: Version 2.0 was released on February 4, 2025.

excerpt: Version 1.0 (May 17, 2024)
paraphrase: Version 1.0 was released on May 17, 2024.

excerpt: Frontier AI Models or Models: are trained on a large data set, display significant generality, are capable of performing a wide range of distinctive tasks and have high-impact capabilities.
paraphrase: Frontier AI models are defined as large, generally capable models able to perform a wide range of distinctive tasks with high-impact capabilities.

context_stem: Frontier AI Models or Models definition
excerpt: Frontier AI models' agentic and reasoning-based general capabilities near or exceed those of other Google models.
paraphrase: Frontier models' agentic and reasoning capabilities approach or surpass those of other Google models.

context_stem: Frontier AI Models or Models definition
excerpt: There may be many different checkpoints and versions of the same model along the entire model lifecycle: we consider checkpoints and versions the same model if their base capabilities stem primarily from the same foundational training run, but will conduct additional testing on new versions as specified in Section 1.3.
paraphrase: Checkpoints and versions sharing the same foundational training run are treated as the same model, though new versions still undergo additional testing per Section 1.3.

context_stem: Frontier AI Models or Models definition
excerpt: When we refer to "model" in this Framework, we may be referring to a checkpoint or version of the model.
paraphrase: The term "model" in the Framework may denote a checkpoint or version of the model.

excerpt: CBRN: risks of models assisting in the development, preparation, and/or execution of a chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear ("CBRN") threat.
paraphrase: CBRN risk refers to models aiding the development, preparation, or execution of chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear threats.

excerpt: Cyber: risks of models assisting in the development, preparation, and/or execution of a cyber attack.
paraphrase: Cyber risk refers to models aiding the development, preparation, or execution of a cyber attack.

excerpt: Harmful Manipulation: risks of models with high manipulative capabilities potentially being misused in ways that could reasonably result in large scale harm.
paraphrase: Harmful Manipulation risk concerns highly manipulative models being misused to cause large-scale harm.

locator: Glossary / Risk Domains / ML R&D and Misalignment
excerpt: ML R&D and Misalignment: risks of models' ML R&D capabilities or misaligned propensities reducing society's overall ability to manage AI risks.
paraphrase: ML R&D and Misalignment risk concerns model capabilities or propensities that reduce society's overall ability to manage AI risks.

locator: Glossary / Risk Domains / ML R&D and Misalignment
excerpt: Such capabilities may serve as a substantial cross-cutting risk factor for several pathways (e.g. through misalignment, misuse or structural risks) to severe harm.
paraphrase: These capabilities can act as a significant cross-cutting factor across multiple pathways to severe harm, including misalignment, misuse, and structural risks.

excerpt: Critical Capability Levels (CCLs): are the main capability thresholds around which we have built the Framework process.
paraphrase: CCLs are the main capability thresholds structuring the Framework process.

excerpt: They represent the capability levels at which, absent mitigation measures, frontier AI models or systems may pose heightened risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: CCLs mark capability levels at which, without mitigations, frontier models could pose heightened risk of severe harm.

excerpt: Tracked Capability Levels (TCLs): are capability thresholds which capture a lower level of risks than our CCLs.
paraphrase: TCLs are capability thresholds representing lower risk levels than CCLs.

excerpt: They represent the capability levels at which, absent mitigation measures, frontier AI models or systems may pose heightened risk of significant but not severe levels of harm.
paraphrase: TCLs mark capability levels at which, without mitigations, frontier models could pose heightened risk of significant but not severe harm.

excerpt: Alert Thresholds: are thresholds which we set marginally earlier than our CCLs.
paraphrase: Alert Thresholds are set slightly ahead of the CCLs.

excerpt: Crossing these thresholds indicates a CCL may be reached in the foreseeable future, due to the speed of capability progress.
paraphrase: Crossing an alert threshold signals that a CCL might be reached soon, given the pace of capability progress.

excerpt: In particular, they are meant to account for the possibility of models reaching a CCL before the next critical capability assessment cycle.
paraphrase: Alert thresholds are designed to account for models potentially reaching a CCL before the next assessment cycle.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Inherent Risk Assessments
excerpt: Inherent Risk Assessments: the process of evaluating the level of risk posed by the model.
paraphrase: Inherent Risk Assessments evaluate the level of risk posed by a model.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Inherent Risk Assessments
excerpt: This is part of the risk management process, and includes material capability change assessments and critical capability assessments.
paraphrase: Inherent Risk Assessments are part of the risk management process and include material capability change assessments and critical capability assessments.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Critical Capability Assessments
excerpt: Critical Capability Assessments: determine a model's proximity to T/CCLs through the use of early warning evaluations and other sources of evidence.
paraphrase: Critical Capability Assessments determine how close a model is to T/CCLs, using early warning evaluations and other evidence.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Early Warning Evaluations
excerpt: Early Warning Evaluations: are evaluations which measure the dangerous capabilities of a model.
paraphrase: Early Warning Evaluations measure a model's dangerous capabilities.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Early Warning Evaluations
excerpt: They specifically target the threats and risk scenarios identified through our threat modeling to determine a model's proximity to a CCL or TCL, and they provide the most direct evidence for whether these thresholds have been reached.
paraphrase: These evaluations target threat-modeled risk scenarios to gauge a model's proximity to a CCL or TCL and give the most direct evidence of whether such thresholds are met.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Material Capability Change Assessments
excerpt: Material Capability Change Assessments: indicate whether a critical capability assessment is required.
paraphrase: Material Capability Change Assessments determine whether a critical capability assessment is needed.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Material Capability Change Assessments
excerpt: These assessments are typically conducted upon the completion of new post-training runs on various checkpoints, and they are primarily aimed at determining whether updated versions of a model have developed material capability increases relative to the last checkpoint subject to a critical capability assessment.
paraphrase: These assessments typically occur after new post-training runs and aim to determine whether updated model versions show material capability increases relative to the last assessed checkpoint.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Material Capability Change Assessments
excerpt: May also be used to assess whether a critical capability assessment is required of non-frontier AI models.
paraphrase: These assessments can also be used to decide whether non-frontier AI models need a critical capability assessment.

locator: Glossary / Inherent Risk Assessment / Material Capability Increases
excerpt: Material Capability Increases: are meaningful new capabilities or material increases in model performance that we believe could materially undermine our justifications for a model's level of risk being acceptable, for example, by reaching a CCL that the previous version of the model had not reached.
paraphrase: Material Capability Increases are significant new capabilities or performance gains believed capable of undermining the justification for a model's risk acceptability, such as reaching a previously unreached CCL.

excerpt: Response Plans: are plans put in place when a new alert threshold has been reached to prepare for future models reaching a CCL.
paraphrase: Response Plans are established once a new alert threshold is reached, to prepare for future models reaching a CCL.

excerpt: Central to most response plans will be the application of the mitigations described earlier in the Framework.
paraphrase: Most response plans center on applying the mitigations described earlier in the Framework.

excerpt: However, if we assess that risks stemming from the model remain acceptable and model capabilities remain distant from a CCL, the response plan may include updating the alert threshold to ensure the safety buffer remains appropriate.
paraphrase: If model risks remain acceptable and capabilities stay distant from a CCL, the response plan may instead update the alert threshold to preserve an appropriate safety buffer.

excerpt: Deployment Mitigations: are safety measures we implement which are intended to counter the misuse or misaligned expression of critical capabilities in deployments.
paraphrase: Deployment Mitigations are safety measures intended to counter misuse or misaligned expression of critical capabilities during deployment.

excerpt: They may include safety post-training, input/output/chain-of-thought monitoring and analysis, account moderation, jailbreak detection and patching, user verification, and bug bounties.
paraphrase: Examples include safety post-training, monitoring of inputs/outputs/chain-of-thought, account moderation, jailbreak detection and patching, user verification, and bug bounties.

excerpt: External Deployments: represent model releases to entities outside of Google.
paraphrase: External Deployments are model releases made to entities outside Google.

excerpt: They can include both low-risk external deployments as well as general purpose releases to the broader public.
paraphrase: External deployments encompass both low-risk external releases and general-purpose public releases.

locator: Glossary / Risk Mitigation / Low-Risk External Deployments
excerpt: Low-Risk External Deployments: represent small scale and private releases restricted to particular external groups or organizations.
paraphrase: Low-Risk External Deployments are small-scale, private releases limited to specific external groups or organizations.

excerpt: Internal Deployments: represent model releases restricted to Google employees for internal use.
paraphrase: Internal Deployments are model releases limited to Google employees for internal use.

locator: Glossary / Risk Mitigation / High-Risk Internal Deployments
excerpt: High-Risk Internal Deployments: represent model releases restricted to Google employees for use cases with the potential to enable severe threat scenarios (e.g. building internal security infrastructure or automating ML R&D).
paraphrase: High-Risk Internal Deployments are releases limited to Google employees for use cases that could enable severe threat scenarios, such as building internal security infrastructure or automating ML R&D.

excerpt: Security Mitigations: are safety measures we implement which are intended to prevent the unauthorized modification or exfiltration of model weights by unauthorized actors.
paraphrase: Security Mitigations are safety measures aimed at preventing unauthorized modification or exfiltration of model weights.

excerpt: They may include identity and access management practices, and hardening interface-access to unreleased model parameters, among other measures.
paraphrase: Examples include identity and access management practices and hardening interface access to unreleased model parameters, among others.

excerpt: We communicate the level of security we consider appropriate to models which cross our thresholds using the RAND model weight security framework.
paraphrase: The appropriate security level for models crossing thresholds is communicated using the RAND model weight security framework.

locator: Glossary / Risk Mitigation / RAND Security Levels
excerpt: RAND Security Levels: indicate security goals and principles relevant to frontier developers aiming to protect their model weights from various actors - with the strength and type of security measures differing for each category of actor.14
paraphrase: RAND Security Levels indicate security goals and principles for frontier developers protecting model weights, with measures varying by actor category.

excerpt: See https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RRA2849-1.html.
paraphrase: Footnote 14 cites a RAND research report URL.

locator: Glossary / Residual Risk Assessment / Residual Risk Assessments
excerpt: Residual Risk Assessments: the process of evaluating the level of risk that remains after all planned mitigation strategies have been implemented.
paraphrase: Residual Risk Assessments evaluate the risk remaining after planned mitigations have been implemented.

locator: Glossary / Residual Risk Assessment / Residual Risk Assessments
excerpt: This is part of the risk management process, following a critical capability assessment and the effect of mitigations.
paraphrase: Residual Risk Assessments are part of the risk management process, occurring after a critical capability assessment and application of mitigations.

locator: Glossary / Residual Risk Assessment / Residual Risk Assessments
excerpt: The residual risk should be brought within the acceptable levels, as determined by the T/CCLs as relevant.
paraphrase: Residual risk is expected to be reduced to acceptable levels as determined by the relevant T/CCLs.

locator: Glossary / Residual Risk Assessment / Safety Cases
excerpt: Safety Cases: are an assessable argument showing how severe risks associated with a model's CCLs have been reduced to an acceptable level.
paraphrase: Safety Cases are assessable arguments demonstrating that severe risks tied to a model's CCLs have been reduced to acceptable levels.

locator: Glossary / Residual Risk Assessment / Safety Cases
excerpt: Residual risk assessments will be supplemented with a safety case when a model reaches a CCL, and inform a model's risk acceptance determination.15
paraphrase: When a model reaches a CCL, residual risk assessments are supplemented with a safety case, which informs the risk acceptance determination.

locator: Glossary / Residual Risk Assessment / Safety Cases
excerpt: For misuse risk, such an argument may be based, for example, on considerations such as the effectiveness of mitigations, the scope of the deployment, what capabilities and mitigations are available on other publicly available models, and the historical incidence and severity of related events.
paraphrase: For misuse risk, a safety case may draw on mitigation effectiveness, deployment scope, capabilities and mitigations of other public models, and the historical incidence and severity of related events.

locator: Glossary / Residual Risk Assessment / Safety Cases
excerpt: For ML R&D and misalignment risk, such an argument may be based, for example, on considerations such as the effectiveness of mitigations relative to model capabilities, and information pertaining to model propensities and the severity of related events.
paraphrase: For ML R&D and misalignment risk, a safety case may draw on mitigation effectiveness relative to model capabilities, model propensity information, and the severity of related events.

excerpt: See also, for reference, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01420.
paraphrase: Footnote 15 cites an arXiv reference for further information.
